question: When the analysis of population density is done by calculating it through net cultivated area, then the measure is termed as:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Physiological density**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Physiological density is a measure of population density that refers to the number of people per unit area of arable land.
 
• This measure provides insights into the pressure exerted by the population on the productive land area.
 
• It helps in understanding the carrying capacity of the land and the potential challenges in terms of food production and resource management.
 
• Physiological density is considered more meaningful than simple population density (people per total land area) because it focuses on the land that can actually support human life.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Agricultural Density**

 
 
• Agricultural density is a measure of the number of farmers per unit area of arable land.
 
• This metric helps in understanding the agricultural efficiency and the potential output of the farming sector.
 
• It provides insights into the level of development and technological advancement in agriculture within a region.
 
• Higher agricultural density may indicate less mechanization and more labor-intensive agriculture.
 
 
 
• **Gross Density**
 
 
• Gross density refers to the total population divided by the total land area.
 
• This measure does not differentiate between arable and non-arable land, giving an overall view of population distribution.
 
• It is useful for general demographic studies and urban planning purposes.
 
• However, it may not accurately reflect the actual human impact on the productive land resources.
 
 
 
• **Net Density**
 
 
• Net density is a less commonly used term and is not a standard measure in population geography.
 
• It might refer to a refined measure of population density considering specific criteria or exclusions.
 
• In most contexts, "net density" is not clearly defined or widely recognized.
 
• It is important to refer to more standardized measures like physiological or agricultural density for accurate analysis.
